reproduction_target: Trends in narrow-/broad-sense heritability, predictive ability (PA) and prediction accuracy (PACC) as a function of SNP subset size (500 -> full set, 1000-SNP intervals, 5 resampling replicates) under ABLUP-AD vs GBLUP-AD individual-tree mixed models, for black spruce (16,207 SNPs / 918 trees), white spruce (10,289 SNPs / 988 trees) and Norway spruce (116,219 SNPs / 1370 trees). Result objects: Table 2, Tables S1-S3, Figs 1-3, Figs S4-S5.
granularity_note: Stage-1 prose triage. Steps derived from named tool/function invocations in Methods sections 2.1-2.4 (guide Step 1, 'else' branch: one step per named tool invocation). No workflow file, no code repository exists, so no objective workflow-derived step list is available; |S| is therefore prose-bound and inter-rater variance on |S| is expected. Field/lab work (trial establishment and sampling, phenotyping incl. X-ray densitometry and Hitman ST300 acoustics, SNP array / exome-capture genotyping) scoped as W (OOS).

steps.label: SNP quality filtering and Mendelian-segregation QC (call rate >= 90%, genotyping reproducibility >= 95%, |Fe| <= 0.50, MAF >= 0.01, >= 5% genotyping-error exclusion, Fisher exact test P < 0.001 in > 3 families); tool not named
Pedigree-based additive relationship matrix A (AGHmatrix::Amatrix) and its inverse (ASRgenomics::G.inverse), per species
Realized additive genomic relationship matrix Ga (ASRgenomics::G.matrix, VanRaden 2008), blending with A (also tested at 0.05 and 0.01), inversion via base R solve()

Dominance relationship matrices: D (AGHmatrix::Amatrix) with inverse via nadiv::makeD; marker-based Gd (ASRgenomics::G.matrix, Vitezica et al. 2013 parametrization) blended with D and inverted via ASRgenomics::G.inverse

SNP subset construction: random draws in 1000-SNP intervals from 500 SNPs to the full set, 5 replicates per subset (up to 20 replicates for height and wood density in white/Norway spruce); one random ramet per clone retained for black spruce. No RNG seed reported

Individual-tree linear mixed models ABLUP-AD and GBLUP-AD fitted in ASReml-R version 4 under R 4.3.2 (site fixed; block-within-site, plot-within-site, additive-within-site, dominance-within-site random; heterogeneous site variances; Eqs 2-3, effects in Table 1)
Across-site variance-component recovery and calculation of narrow-sense heritability, dominance ratio, broad-sense heritability and type-B genetic correlations (Eqs 4-7)

10-fold within-family cross-validation of GS models (folds balanced within family, one random ramet per clone for black spruce), recovery of EBV/EDV/EGV BLUPs, and computation of predictive ability (PA) and prediction accuracy (PACC) per site then averaged over sites and repetitions. No RNG seed reported

Field material: progeny trials for black spruce (2 sites, 918 trees, 34 families), white spruce (2 sites, 988 trees, 56 families) and Norway spruce (2 sites, 1370 trees, 128 families); establishment, maintenance, sampling
Phenotyping: height, DBH, X-ray densitometry wood density (Quintek Measurement Systems), Pilodyn pin penetration, acoustic velocity (Hitman ST300)
SNP genotyping: Infinium iSelect Pmr25k and PgLM3+ arrays (black/white spruce); exome capture on Illumina HiSeq 2500 (Norway spruce, Chen et al. 2018)

gaps.missing: Phenotyping and genotyping data are explicitly not deposited in the public domain, citing Intellectual Property Policies of participating governmental and private organizations. No accession, no repository, no DOI. Access is discretionary: 'data will be shared upon motivated request to the corresponding author after consulting with participating governmental and private organizations involved in this work.' There is no named data access committee, no documented decision criteria and no stated turnaround, so this is not a controlled-access path that a reproducer can rely on.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit genotype matrices and phenotype tables under a formal controlled-access repository (EGA / dbGaP / a Dataverse restricted collection) with a resolvable accession and a documented DAC procedure, or deposit the derived relationship matrices and per-fold prediction tables that are sufficient to re-run the modelling steps without releasing individual-tree IP-restricted data.

gaps.missing: No code availability statement and no analysis code deposited anywhere. No GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Zenodo/Software Heritage link appears in the manuscript. The R/ASReml-R scripts that build the relationship matrices, run the SNP-subset resampling loop, fit the mixed models and perform the 10-fold cross-validation are not linked.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the R driver scripts (matrix construction, resampling loop, ASReml-R model specifications, CV harness, PA/PACC computation) in a public repository with a Zenodo DOI and cite it in a Code Availability Statement.

gaps.missing: The QC step names no software at all - the thresholds (call rate, reproducibility rate, |Fe|, MAF, Mendelian-error rate, Fisher exact test) are given but the implementing tool/script is neither named nor deposited. White-spruce filtering is delegated by reference to Nadeau et al. (2023).
gaps.how_to_close: Name the genotype-calling and filtering software (e.g. GenomeStudio version, or the custom R script) and deposit the filtering script together with the SNP inclusion/exclusion lists per species.

gaps.missing: 2a - no versions given for the R packages AGHmatrix, ASRgenomics and nadiv. 2b - ASReml-R is pinned only to major series ('version 4'), which is a floating lower bound across the 4.x line. Only the interpreter is pinned exactly (R 4.3.2). No CRAN snapshot date, no renv.lock, no container.
gaps.how_to_close: Report exact package versions and a CRAN/Posit-PPM snapshot date, or ship an renv.lock (or Docker image digest) covering R 4.3.2 plus AGHmatrix, ASRgenomics, nadiv and the ASReml-R build.

gaps.missing: ASReml-R version 4 is commercial, licence-gated software. Every model fit and every cross-validation round depends on it; a reproducer without a licence cannot execute these steps as described.
gaps.how_to_close: Provide an open-source equivalent specification (e.g. sommer / BGLR / MTG2 model code producing the same variance-component decomposition) alongside the ASReml-R code, or at minimum record the exact ASReml-R build and licence class.

gaps.where: Methods 2.4.2 (SNP subset resampling), 2.4.4 (fold assignment and ramet choice)
gaps.missing: Three stochastic operations - random SNP draws per subset size (5 replicates, up to 20 for the sufficiency check), random 10-fold within-family assignment, and the random choice of one ramet per black-spruce clone - are reported without any RNG seed or seeding scheme. Only the between-replicate standard deviation is reported.
gaps.how_to_close: Report set.seed values (or the seed list per replicate) in the deposited script; failing that, results can only ever be checked for distributional agreement, not point agreement.

gaps.missing: Trial establishment, 13-33 year field maintenance, destructive wood coring, X-ray densitometry, Pilodyn and acoustic-velocity measurement, and SNP array / exome-capture genotyping are non-computational and out of scope for a reproduction attempt (scored OOS, excluded from |S|).
gaps.how_to_close: Not applicable - documentation-audit only. The methods are described at a level consistent with the field-genetics literature and reference prior publications (Lenz et al. 2017, Nadeau et al. 2023, Chen et al. 2018, Gerardi et al. 2025).
